title.narrative: Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project - Phase 1

description.narrative: The Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project - Phase 1 (the project) will reduce climate risks and enable climate adaptation in three major river basins (the Abra River basin in Luzon, and the Ranao [Agus] and Tagum-Libuganon river basins in Mindanao), with a focus on addressing flood risk. The project will enhance flood and climate change resilience by (i) improving strategic flood risk management planning, (ii) constructing flood protection infrastructure, and (iii) strengthening community-based flood risk management.

description.narrative: Flood risk in three river basins reduced

150 barangays in the three river basins have reduced flood and climate risks Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Initial engagements have been conducted with 5 LGUs in TLRB and 3 LGUs in ARB which will guide work with their corresponding barangays. Data Source: Reports from disaster management unit (DRRM offices of LGUs)

3,800 hectares of agricultural land protected from 1-in-50-year flood event and 1,600 hectares protected from erosion risks Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Four contracts (2 Agus and 2 Abra) were awarded in Jun-Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 respectively. For the Tagum package, requirements are being completed by the contractor to allow for contract signing. Data Source: Flood modeling reports, PPMS and annual reports

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Community-based flood risk management strengthened Indicator: At least 500 LGU staff and local civil society organization or community representatives, of which at least 30% are women and including indigenous cultural community representatives, have improved knowledge and awareness of flood risks Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: PIC will engage local civil society organizations to implement the community-based flood risk management component. This will involve supporting and facilitating the assessment of local flood and climate risks, integrating flood risk considerations into local development plans (gender-responsive), and conducting capacity-building programs and policy reviews to strengthen local flood risk management capabilities. Data Source: PPMS and QPRs

Output: Community-based flood risk management strengthened Indicator: Flood risk management mainstreamed in community-based DRRM plans for 150 barangays in the three river basins and are made gender-responsive and with elements of universal design Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Initial engagements have been conducted with 5 LGUs in TLRB and 3 LGUs in ARB which will guide work with their corresponding barangays. Next step include the convening of Barangay Development Councils (BDC) and Barangay DRRMCs, which will support planning workshops and subsequent mentoring for the preparation of CBDRRMPs. Data Source: PPMS and QPRs

Output: Community-based flood risk management strengthened Indicator: Flood risk management mainstreamed in local development plans for 22 LGUs in the three river basins and are made gender-responsive and with elements of universal design Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Initial coordination meetings have already been conducted with 5 LGUs in TLRB and 3 LGUs in ARB to establish early groundwork for incorporating gender‑responsive and universal design elements into local planning processes. Next steps include the creation of a Technical Working Group, engagement of experts/resource persons, and conduct of CDRA training to advance FRM mainstreaming in the LGUs. Data Source: PPMS and QPRs

Output: Community-based flood risk management strengthened Indicator: Gender-sensitive and culturally appropriate information, education, and communication materials for flood risk management provided to 22 LGUs and 150 barangays in the three river basin communities Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: PIC will engage local civil society organizations to implement the community-based flood risk management component. This will involve supporting and facilitating the assessment of local flood and climate risks, integrating flood risk considerations into local development plans (gender-responsive), and conducting capacity-building programs and policy reviews to strengthen local flood risk management capabilities. Data Source: PPMS and QPRs

Output: Flood protection infrastructure constructed Indicator: At least 20% of the workforce employed in structural and nonstructural (administrative, logistics) works program is female Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: At the Agus 1 site, initial workforce data shows that female workers account for 19% of the 160 personnel. Data Source: PPMS, QPRs, and surveys; and Procurement and contract management database

Output: Flood protection infrastructure constructed Indicator: Structural flood protection and mitigation infrastructure in the three river basins rehabilitated, upgraded, or constructed at 51 sites, with nature-based approaches adopted Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 4 works contracts awarded: Agus 1 (Jun 2025), Agus 2 (Aug 2025), Abra 1 and 2 (Nov 2025). The Tagum contract will be signed after documents/requirements are completed by the contractor. The project implementation consultants will provide construction supervision. Data Source: Detailed design reports, PPMS, QPRs, and surveys; and Procurement and contract management database

Output: Strategic flood risk management planning improved Indicator: Department of Public Works and Highways' capacity-building program for flood risk management planning established and strengthened, with 20 trainers trained Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The Capacity Building Unit (CBU) was formed to lead the preparation and implementation of the capacity‑building program. 52 participants have been identified for the training of trainers. The overall concept of the capacity‑building program is being prepared for CBU review, and a technical program has already been developed for finalization with the CBU. Training Needs Assessment instruments for ToT participants completed and monitoring and evaluation tools being developed. Data Source: PPMS and QPRs

Output: Strategic flood risk management planning improved Indicator: Two X-band radar rainfall gauges installed and operationalized Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: DPWH and PAGASA visited two proposed locations for X‑band radar installation (one in Marawi and one in Abra). PAGASA will prepare the radar specifications once the final installation sites are confirmed. Preparation of bidding document and procurement will proceed after the specifications are finalized. Data Source: Procurement and contract award database

Output: Strategic flood risk management planning improved Indicator: AMIS-FRM with supporting inventories of assets for the three river basins developed and operationalized Achievement: N Progress/Status: An AMIS‑FRM design workshop, held on 12-13 August 2025, discussed existing DPWH applications, system specifications, functionalities, expected outputs, and sustainability requirements. This resulted in revisions to the TOR of the AMIS‑FRM developer. The TOR is being reviewed by FCMC and several other DPWH offices and will be submitted to ADB for review.
